title: Stalled on‑prem upgrade due to KV cache schema mismatch — safe repair and hotfix rollout
creator: Aisha Verma
description: During a rolling operator/Helm upgrade for a Private (VPC/on‑prem) customer cluster we observed a class of upgrades stall and enter reconcile loops. Root cause traced to a KV cache schema change in the nodeagent/operator handshake that was applied mid‑upgrade, producing incompatible cache projections and causing controller reconcile crashes and scheduling pressure. This ticket tracks emergency mitigation, hotfix release, and safer upgrade primitives to prevent recurrence.
reproduction_steps: Provision a small onprem test cluster with nodeagent v1.7.9 and operator v1.7.9
Deploy sample workload that keeps KV cache warm (long lived chat sessions) and enable autoscaling
Trigger Helm operator upgrade to operator v1.8.0 and nodeagent v1.8.0 in same release
Observe operator post‑upgrade hooks applying CRD changes while nodeagent performs an on‑disk KV cache migration
Watch operator reconcile enter crashloop: stack shows marshal/unmarshal errors for KV entries with old schema tags
investigation_summary: Initial telemetry from customer cluster showed reconcile restarts coinciding with helm post‑upgrade hook execution. Logs contained JSON unmarshal errors in operator reconcile: the new operator expected a 'session_v2' field that nodeagent had not yet populated. The nodeagent had begun an async on‑disk migration of the KV cache; under high load this migration delayed stabilization, leaving operator instances to observe mixed schema entries. The operator code path lacked a backward‑compatibility shim for the older schema and attempted optimistic compaction which triggered a reconcile failure and subsequent cascade of resource requeues causing API server pressure. CPU and disk IO spiked during the migration leading to delayed liveness probes and pod restarts.
